transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Well, I'm here because... I guess what finally made me come in and actually say something is that, after I eat too much, I’ve been going upstairs and making myself throw up. Then I just come back down and act as if I’m just tidying the kitchen or getting ready for bed. I just realized it's getting out of hand and I needed to talk to someone about it.

When you say you 'eat too much' before making yourself throw up, can you describe what that's like—are you eating a much larger amount of food than most people would in that time, and do you feel like you can't stop or control it while it's happening?

Yes, it's definitely a much larger amount. When no one else is in the kitchen, I can just... I can go through all the leftovers from a church supper, plus crackers, cheese, cookies, and whatever I might have baked for my book club, all in one sitting. It's far more than I would ever actually serve myself at a normal meal. And yes, once I start doing that, it really does feel like I just can't stop myself or control it.
Can you tell me your current height and weight, and whether you feel you are underweight, average, or overweight right now?

I honestly couldn't tell you my exact height and weight right now. I haven't stepped on a scale or been measured in quite a long time. And as for how I feel... I'm not really sure. I guess it's hard for me to judge if I'm average or overweight at this point. I just don't have a very good sense of it right now.
On average, how many times per week have you been binge eating and then making yourself throw up, and how many months has this pattern been going on?

Well, this has been going on since last winter. I'd say there has hardly been a single week since then where I haven’t had at least one of those private eating spells. And then, you know, I try to make up for it... usually by throwing up, like I mentioned, or sometimes I'll just skip meals or really overdo my walking to try and compensate. So, it's been at least once a week for almost a year now.
Have people around you, like family or your doctor, ever expressed concern that you look very thin or underweight?

Yes, actually. My daughter mentioned it recently, and a woman from my church also told me I look too thin. But... I don't know, it just doesn't feel that way to me. I still panic if my skirt feels even a little snug, or if the scale goes up even a single pound. It's like I immediately feel as if I've somehow let myself become huge overnight, regardless of what they say.
Would you be willing to have your height and weight measured here today so we can calculate your current BMI together?

I guess I could do that. I mean, I'm not exactly thrilled about the idea of getting on a scale right now, but... if you think it's necessary for us to figure out where I'm at, then yes, I'm willing to be measured.
Have you noticed any changes in your menstrual cycle, such as periods becoming irregular or stopping altogether, since this pattern began?

Well, I'm 56, so... my periods actually stopped a few years ago because of menopause. So, no, I haven't noticed any changes like that related to the eating, since I haven't had a cycle for a while anyway.
Now that we're here together, let's go ahead and get your height and weight measured—can you step on the scale for me so we can calculate your BMI?
Alright. Let me just take my shoes off. ... Okay, I'm on.
Now that we have your height and weight, your BMI comes out to [value] — can we go over that number together and see how it compares to a healthy weight range for your height?

Yes, we can do that. I mean... I'm not exactly looking forward to talking about the number, to be completely honest with you, but... yeah, we can go over it. I know it's something we need to look at. How does it compare?
Your BMI today calculated out to a specific number—can you tell me what that number was, and does it fall below 18.5?

Well, you just calculated it, so you have the exact number in front of you. I didn't actually see the screen. I know my weight is usually normal, or maybe a bit above average, so I don't think my BMI would be below 18.5... but you'd have to tell me what it actually said.
